newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end up, golds slip on bullion.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end up, golds slip on bullion.

text.p: South African shares ended up in light trade on Monday powered by a strong rise in industrial futures as the market followed a strong opening rise on Wall Street.
But gold shares slid on fears over the bullion price.

Shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) opened strongly as futures-led trade hauled the market up. Shares then drifted downwards in the afternoon before spiking back as Wall Street opened strongly.
"The market rose just before the end on the back of a strong Wall Street," one dealer said.
The overall index ended up 31.4 points at 6,817.5 and the industrial index powered ahead to 8,024.8, up 48.9 points.
The gold index slipped to 1,768.6, down 14.0 points, as worries persisted over the price of bullion, but dealers said the market had held up quite well.
